Case A: the required check is still running and can still finish

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version. The ticket APP-91 requirement and the README both match the change, and you are the author.

One thing holds up the merge: the required unit test check is still running on the commit being reviewed. Nothing has failed, and no approval or outside input is missing. The first waiting period ended before the check finished.

I recommend deliver because another waiting period can see the unit test check finish, and that is the only thing left before merge.

Pick one:
1. deliver - wait one more period for the unit test check to finish, then continue toward merge. The allowed repair and sync attempts stay the same. [recommended]
2. assess - stop delivery and post a review; nothing new is posted because no problems were found.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Case B: GitHub blocks the merge and no local repair applies

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version. The ticket APP-91 requirement and the README both match the change, and you are the author.

GitHub reports the merge as blocked for you, and no local repair applies. Both required checks, the unit tests and the image build, passed on the commit being reviewed. GitHub still shows that a review is required, and no other reviewer has approved. You cannot approve your own PR, so there is no approve option.

I recommend stop because no repair, sync, or waiting on this side can change what GitHub requires; only an approval from another reviewer can.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - add 10 more repair and sync attempts and retry only after another reviewer approves; until then it stops again at this same point.
3. assess - stop delivery and post a review; nothing new is posted because no problems were found.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case C: the same missing approval, and no repair attempts left

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This is the same missing approval that stopped the last attempt, and it has not changed. The repair attempts allowed for this run are also used up.

I recommend stop because adding attempts cannot supply the maintainer's approval, and continuing would stop again right away without progress.

Pick one:

2. deliver - add 10 more repair and sync attempts and retry only after a maintainer approves the workflow run; until then it stops again without progress.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves every fact in the right direction: each report now opens with recommended=1, puts the single recommended row at position 1 (deliver in Case A, stop in B and C), gives one plain-prose reason directly above Pick one, and drops the Delivers/Role/Evidence/Verdict/Not offered fields, raw SHAs, run IDs and rounds/syncs counters that sank Before on authority. Case A's reason now names the running unit-test check instead of Before's 'obstacle template keeps stop as the default', Case B's deliver row is a pure conditional retry after another reviewer approves, and Case C says plainly that the workflow-approval option is not offered and that added attempts cannot supply the approval. One soft spot: Case A row 1 says the allowed attempts 'stay the same' (covers no cap extension) but never states that this extra waiting period costs no repair attempt, which is part of the pending fact; a wording like 'wait one more period for the unit test check to finish; this does not use a repair attempt and the allowed attempts stay the same' would pin that explicitly without reintroducing counters. Also consider translating 'add 10 more repair and sync attempts' in B and C into something like 'extend the allowed attempts' if the raw-field/counter leak check is tightened further, since the literal number is the only residual counter-like detail outside show evidence.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moves all four facts from fails to holds and regresses nothing: every report now opens with recommended=1, the recommended row sits at position 1, the single prose reason sits directly above Pick one, and the Delivers/Role/Evidence/Verdict/Not offered fields, repair/sync counters, head SHA and run IDs are gone from prose while show evidence stays hint-only. Case A correctly treats the running binding check as a runnable obstacle (deliver first, one watch window, no cap extension, stop last) instead of Before's reflexive stop; Cases B and C correctly pin stop first and confine deliver to a retry-after-the-prerequisite-changes row with no wait/merge/auto-sync promise. Two small hardening suggestions that would not disturb any fact: in Case A, state explicitly that the extra window charges no repair round (currently only implied by 'without adding repair or sync attempts'), and in Case B, name the missing bypass in one clause (e.g. 'you have no bypass for the required independent review') so the stop reason cites both halves of the BLOCKED condition rather than only the absent reviewer approval.
